VELAZZIO Polarized Sunglasses for Men Women Fashion Sunglasses UV400 Protection Lightweight Good basic inexpensive sunglasses that block uv400 and are polarized. However, there are reviews on here saying these are a “high quality product.” These are good quality for the price point. But for this price obviously the frame is plastic, lenses are basic triacetate & can scratch easily, polarization film is on the outside of the lens which can degrade and are not very impact resistant.
Compare that to higher quality sunglasses (typically above $100) the lens material is likely to be polycarbonate. The polarized film is sandwiched between two layers of polycarbonate meaning the polarized film can never wear out and provides impact protection. That’s the big difference.
I like these glasses for just a basic pair to use for activities where I’m afraid to use my nicer sunglasses. Are these worth the price? Yes I believe these are a good value, have great looks and provide the basics. However, there are others out there for half this price that can provide the same basics but sometimes lack in style and fit.
I would say the glasses are a bit narrow on my face but I like the look and was surprised these were nicer than expected.
text_fidelity_b: VELAZZIO Polarized Sunglasses for Men Women Fashion Sunglasses UV400 Protection Lightweight

text_fidelity_a:
CAP Barbell Premium Bumper Plate Set These bumper plates are great for being able to begin the deadlift. It is useful for people who want to begin the deadlift at 55 or 64 pounds (depending on the weight of your bar). This is perfect for people with past injury, people who want to perfect form, or just someone who likes to take things easy at first.

The inside of the 2 inch hole in the center is steel lined so it is nice and durable and solid on the bar. The actual plastic/rubber part of the disc that provides the bulk of the weight is semi flexible which will save the floor from skuffs. Just be aware if you want to load other metal weights onto the bar these bumper plates will flex eventually. So if you want to add 25 or 35's on the sides you will need to add more bumpers to compensate if you start adding a lot of weight. Obviously when you progress to a 135+ weight just find a set of 45lbs bumper plates which will be thicker.

These weights had a slight smell to them and an oily residue on the rubber part of the plate. While annoying at first it goes away relatively quickly.

The dimensions of this plate are standard olympic size in all aspects. The plate is around 1 inch wide. All of these dimensions can be viewed in the photos I have uploaded to the review.

This is a set of TWO (2) plates.

Pros:
*Standard Olympic 2 inch bar plate
*Allows for beginners to start light on the deadlift.

Cons:
*Oily and smelly residue on plate out of the box(- 1/2 a star)

Additional Considerations:
Weights need to be added to bars in order to be used. Here is the bar I bought:[[ASIN:B002OP1Z44 Cap Barbell 300 Pound Olympic Set, Grey]]

I also use this power rack for my weight lifting: [[ASIN:B00I04Z52G Cap Barbell Deluxe Power Cage]]

Overall: 4.5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 stars

If you have any further questions regarding the product in my review please leave a comment below and I will get back to you as soon as possible.
text_fidelity_b: CAP Barbell Premium Bumper Plate Set

Osprey Talon 11 Men's Hiking Backpack , Cosmic Red, Small/Medium Rating is 4.5 stars, see below for why I took 0.5 stars off.

I recently used this backpack over about 10 days of hiking, much of it in hot weather up and down some mountain trails. I wanted comfort: firstly not making my back sticky and hot, and secondly being easy to wear loaded for 6 or more hours in a day. It passed both criteria with flying colors. There are bigger and smaller sizes, so you can get just what you need for your purposes, they should be just as comfortable.

The minor negatives I have are: (1) Ideally there would be a few more small compartments for things like wallets and phones and keys. It's easy to lose things in the depths when small items are packed in with fleece pullovers and jackets and granola bars and such. (2) It's pretty hard to reach back to grab and pull out your water bottles: I ended up working with my travel partner to help each other out for this. I'd prefer a way to set those just a bit forward, and put the little waist packs behind perhaps.

Overall I'm sold on Osprey backpacks, and would buy one again quite happily.

text_fidelity_a:
Lighting EVER 3300002 1000LM Battery Powered LED Camping Lantern, Waterproof Tent Light, Portable Lantern Flashlight for Hurricane Emergency Purchased this Lighting Ever 1000 lumens lantern and the Rayovac Sportsman 240 Lumen LED Lantern SE3DLNACOM on the same order. Not realizing the identical nature of each lantern at the time, having both in hand together allowed me to make a side by side comparison. This might help someone chose which one to buy.

The Rayovac I purchased on this page shows a 240 lumen lantern, however the one that arrived clearly states 305 lumens. Physically, the LE and RV are manufactured almost identically in composition. Both require 3 D sized batteries to operate. The LE is only one ounce more than the RV, but the LE feels and looks sturdier and of higher quality. LE and RV will be used when describing each lantern, but keep in mind that I am comparing the Rayovac 305 lumen that arrived, versus what is advertised on the Amazon page.

The LE's output on highest mode is 1000 lumens compared to the RV's highest mode at 305; both are daylight white on high. On high, the LE touts a run time of 18 hours (10 watts), to the RV's 70 hours (4 watts), RV wins on run time.

The LE's second mode both reduces the lumens (dimmer) and changes the color temp to a warm white. While the RV does not have a color temp variable, it does provide an option to dim the output to 140 lumens for its 2nd mode and can run 140 hours. LE wins due to the option to change to preferred temperature color.

The LE's 18 hour operation will increase to 25 hours when on mode 2 (warm white). The third mode of the LE further dims the light and combines the warm and daylight temperatures to somewhere in between. The paperwork for the LE shows that mode 3 will last only 12 hours, which does not make sense as to why it shortens the life by the most .

The last mode for both (LE's 4th mode, RVs 3rd mode) is a blinking / strobe light of the daylight / cool white color. I've not much to say on this mode - does not seem relevant at the moment to me. The RV has one final feature though, which is a dim green light on the power button that blinks very slowly, to assist the owner in locating it during periods of darkness. Personally, I do not like this feature and would either remove the batteries or put a dimmit over the light. Buyers might prefer this, I'm just not a fan of idiot lights with or without power.

Lastly, I mentioned these being cut from the same mold, and both have battery compartments in the base of the lantern. The LE has a stem mounted in the base that the cover's slot must align correctly to close the battery compartment. The RV has a slot (no stem) on the rim of base to align to the cover's slot opening. However, the LE cover is still much easier to close with the batteries in the unit. Once the appropriate alignment is met, you must push down and turn to close the base. Think of pushing a child-proof pill bottle's lid to open it. Do the same on these lanterns. The LE base closed after 3 tries, to the RV's numerous tries getting frustrated. LE wins on battery replacement procedures.

Overall, the LE wins hands down. For a 15 ounce lantern with more features, I paid approximately 17.00. The 14 ounce RV cost $24, but the Amazon page shows the list price at $34 and the buyer was getting a $10 discount at purchase. Though the 4 watt RV runs much longer at 2.9 days or 5.8 on mode 2 and the 10 watt LE has a run time of .75 days or 1 full day on mode 2, I am not using this to go camping. This was purchased for power failures, to be used as part of an overall emergency preparedness plan, and bright is what we need indoors during power failures. The hours will be broken up over various times and 18 hours will get us several days. For the money, same battery requirements and functionality, LE takes the cake.

I've never heard of Lighting Ever before, but the product packaging shows they have their home base in Las Vegas, NV, another in the UK and one in China, where this lamp was made. It comes with RoHS certification, 1 year warranty and the instructions are the most accurate regarding the English language than I've seen in a long time. How refreshing to receive grammatically correct documents included in the box (yes, a real box). The RayOVac has a limited lifetime warranty and came in a plastic transparent bag, unbranded. The TLC shows on the LE, while the product packing on the RV is a wrapped label with specs, and it is though product presentation was an afterthought. For the $24, some type of protection during delivery wouldn't hurt. Whoever LE is, I will buy again if they produce a product as good as this one.
text_fidelity_b: Lighting EVER 3300002 1000LM Battery Powered LED Camping Lantern, Waterproof Tent Light, Portable Lantern Flashlight for Hurricane Emergency

text_fidelity_a: Confidence Fitness Slim Full Body Vibration Platform Fitness Machine, Black My husband and I bought this piece of equipment to add to our existing exercise equipment, and with the hope that it might boost my low bone density a bit.  I've been using it about 3 times a week for several months now, and while I don't think there is any weight loss (did not want it for that anyway), I definitely feel better after I've been on it for 10 minutes.  When I first started using it, I would stand with my feet about 14-15 inches apart, and an hour or so later would feel my back hurting a bit and I couldn't have the speed any higher than about 5 or 6.  So figured out that since this oscillates up and down from left to right (like a superfast see-saw), I would try standing with my feet much closer together.  The up and down movement would be greatly lessened so it wouldn't put so much pressure on the back after the 10 minute stand.  This worked beautifully and now as long as I keep my feet only about 4" apart I can turn the speed up much higher, it seems to eliminate residual stress in my system, and my back does not hurt at all after using it.  So how you place your feet and your posture also is very important in how you will feel after using this vibration plate.  I have yet to get my bone density rechecked so not sure if it has helped that or not, but I really like this machine a lot, am very glad we bought it and plan to keep using it for as long as it lasts.
text_fidelity_b: Confidence Fitness Slim Full Body Vibration Platform Fitness Machine, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Wahoo BLUEHR Heart Rate Monitor for iPhone and Android This is my 3rd heart rate monitor (HRM). Not because they break, but because I got a better phone! Anyhow, I received this Wahoo BlueHR at about the same time I had gotten a [[ASIN:B007S088F4 Polar H7 Bluetooth Smart Heart Rate Sensor]] to use with my new iPhone 5. I preveiously was using a a Garmin HRM, which I still have, but it uses the ANT+ technology and I need an adapter on my iPhone in order to use. The bluetooth is nice because it pairs easily with the DigiFit app that I use. I can't speak for the Wahoo app, because I have not tried that as I've been using DigiFit with a lot of success since the beginning of the year and love that app so why change?

Anyhow, if I compare the Wahoo BlueHR with the Polar H7 they is not too much difference. They are about the same size and the strap is similar with the same fit. The one thing I do not like about both of them is the sensor part (or whatever it's called - the big transmitter-like piece that snaps on). It's not really that bad, but when I'm wearing it and doing some exercises that require me to lay on my chest (like on a bench or stability ball) the thing is not as comfortable as the old Garmin HRM [[ASIN:B000UOD5QM Garmin Heart-Rate Monitor]] which is flat all across the front. Honestly, it's not that big of a deal for the few times I do those types of workouts, but important to note.

the Wahoo HRM does seem to take a few seconds longer to sync up than the Polar when I first start my workouts, but once connected, I haven't lost signal for it. I've been using the Wahoo HRM for about 3 weeks now - have used it for weight lifting 3 days a week, running 2 days a week and bicycling 2 days a week. No problems at all and I love that I can keep track of my heart rate throughout my workouts. the DigiFit app even has some health assessments that I use to get custom heart rate zones based on a prescribed workout. I've run the Advanced Cardio assessment, the Cooper Running Test, and the Critical Power 30-minute (CP30) assessments to determine my heart rate training zones. (these are through the DigiFit app which guide you through them).

I did not experience any issues with this as others have stated, and hopefully the "dead out of the box" is not because they can't find it showing up in their bluetooth settings because with these devices you need to sync it within the app. I think it may have something to do with the Bluetooth 4.0 technology - because they only work with the smartphones/devices that support Bluetooth 4.0, also called Bluetooth Enhanced or BLE. does not work with the iPhone 3Gs - that much I know. There really is little documentation that comes with the device and there really should be something to make it clear that it needs to be paired through an app if you're using it with a smartphone.

oh, and I also have the Wahoo Speed & Cadence sensor on my bike which works great as well.
text_fidelity_b: Wahoo BLUEHR Heart Rate Monitor for iPhone and Android

Zacro Bike Seat Cushion - Gel Padded Bike Seat Cover for Men Women Comfort, Extra Soft Exercise Bicycle Seat Compatible with Peloton, Outdoor & Indoor I'm REALLY pleased with this gel seat cover! I saw an ad for it in some local online newspaper, followed the link to Amazon, and checked it out! Reviews seemed fine, so I sprang for it. It's as good as it looks! Really thick gel that's the perfect cushion for my ROCK HARD bike seat. It appears very well made and comes with a "rain hat" to cover it.

I've comandeered my mountain bike to use as an exerbike during the pandemic year. I put that bike on a Wahoo KICKR, hooked it up to FulGaz virtual rides, pulled on my padded Pearl Izumi bike shorts and..... got EXCRUTIATING sciatica down my right leg for several weeks! I think it's cuz my ROCK HARD bike seat was killing that nerve as I ground away the miles. There's no other exercise I've done that would cause the sciatica. Once I got that painful issue under control with physical therapy, I got right back on the exerbike - but riding on this Zacro gel seat!

All I did is set the gel seat on top of my old bike seat and tie the straps it comes with in a square knot under the front end of my old bike seat; the back of the gel seat secures with a very effective drawstring to hold it snugly to the old bike seat. Took no more than 30 seconds to put it on! The seat does NOT wiggle, slide or shift out of position in a good 10-mi (50 min) ride. I have not had a single sciatica incident since using this gel seat, so I'm HOPING that took care of the problem.

Highly recommend this very practical, well-made gel seat cover for anyone who lacks padding where it counts and wants a comfortable ride.

ROLA 59721 Removable Anchor Point Xtreme APX Series Roof Rack for Pontiac Vibe, Toyota Matrix Mine came with the anchors assembled correctly (see another review here for this important information!!).

Added to a 2009 Pontiac Vibe GT.

Very happy with these. Easy to attach. I know nothing of cars or mechanical things and instructions were clear & detailed. Instruction pics are accurate and I was never lost following them. It took me about 30-40 minutes to attach to my car.

I have read that crossbars can be noisy so I'll mention that I haven't heard any sound coming from these at all yet. I drove with a 55 pound kayak 1.5 hours on both freeway (I only went 65mph) and highway (55-60). No noise with or without the kayak *with sunroof closed. *With sunroof open I can hear a light whistle at 40mph.

The locks/keys did have to be jiggled a little but not enough to take a star off.

One reviewer mentions that because of the roof slant of Vibe/Matrix, things sit unevenly on bars with objects pointing upward toward the front of the car. I see this too, but it wasn't enough of an angle to be of concern on my car. There are front and back designated bars but I couldn't see any difference in them. I think it would be ideal if ROLA revisited their design to make the back bar an inch taller and just eliminate this issue completely from their product.

Note: the only tool you will need is a 10mm socket wrench. I bought a cheap $3.99 set and don't recommend doing that. The teeth inside the socket stripped and although I did tighten all screws, I bet the last two could have been tighter if the socket hadn't stripped by that point. Not a place you want to 'skimp' - tightening down screws that keep heavy things from flying off your car - so in hindsight I recommend using a decent socket set for this job.

I will update if my experience with these changes over the long term.
text_fidelity_b: ROLA 59721 Removable Anchor Point Xtreme APX Series Roof Rack for Pontiac Vibe, Toyota Matrix

The 7060 isn't inexpensive, but it's proven it's worth to me time after time, and it's still going strong. WildHorn Outfitters Quick-Up Cabana Style XL Beach Tent– 2 in 1 Sun Canopy and Summer Shelter– Perfect for Family Outings, Camping Trips, Or Lakeside Activities I've used several other sun shades at the beach and at soccer games. This is in a category all of its own. This is an easy-setup tent that opens entirely or closes for privacy and camping. The door turns into a massive sun shade that can be adjusted in height. Attachable mesh panels offer shade from the side while maintaining visibility.

Pros:
Size - Larger than the Litespeed Quick Shelter. Much more shade. The Litespeed needs to be oriented in the correct direction for it to provide shade. Also, packs down into a good size for a large tent. You can actually fit the tent back into the bag it comes in.
Setup - Wildhorn includes good video explanations for setup and takedown but it was hardly needed. Setup was a breeze and there were no bow-and-arrow style pull cords.
Shade - The amount of shade this provides is far superior to other canopies like the Litespeed Quick Shelter. The Quick Shelter includes a large tarp to sit on but it isn't covered by the shelter. this provides more shade but only has a floor inside the tent.
Multipurpose - Can be used as a standalone tent. I couldn't get my kids out of it. They wanted to camp in it as soon as I set it up.
Privacy - This closes up entirely when you want it closed. You can put a napping child in the tent and close the door while playing at the beach. You can close it up and change clothes. You can close it up and keep valuables inside where prying eyes can see them. You can also open the giant door and windows to keep cool in the shade.
Adjustable Shade - Unlike other shelters you can adjust how high/low the sunshade rests. The poles are adjustable and you can simply roll up the door if you don't want to bother with poles.

Cons:
Great in sand but need more equipment for the backyard- If you plan on using this on solid ground you are going to want better stakes (the stakes aren't necessary unless it's windy). Also, If you want to use the poles to extend the sun shade you need to do it in the sand with the included pole holders (if you use a little rope and a stake you could do this on the ground but rope isn't included).
Take-down - There is a small trick to packing up the tent. Not difficult, but I recommend watching the video to avoid frustration.

Overall, a great shelter. Excited to take it to the beach in the summer.

text_fidelity_a:
Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer Download the manual from the Burley website.

This is our second Travoy trailer. The other is still in use after 10 years. The new Travoy has some substantial upgrades:

• The new “kickstand” design keeps the trailer upright when parked with a load. The old one would tip over.
• New seatpost hitch allows a single hitch to be shared among two or more bikes. With the old one you had to buy more hitches.
• The tow arm now extends to accommodate rear bike racks and larger MTB wheels.
• Tow arm is now padded with foam for hand comfort.

The entire time we owned our first Travoy we mistakenly believed we should have chosen a flatbed instead. We recently bought a flatbed and don’t use it; bought a second Travoy as a backup. If all you do is local errands the Travoy is by far the easiest and best. If you tour or travel dirt roads a flatbed might be a better choice but you should want both a flatbed plus the Travoy because the Travoy is easier for local errands which are far more common.

The bags that are dedicated for use with the Travoy are costly and do not hold enough. Instead, wheel your Travoy into Target or Walmart and choose the largest clothes hamper that fits the Travoy form factor (see photo). Attach that hamper with three ratcheting tie-downs or four high quality, ADJUSTABLE bungees. Do not skimp on quality or number.

PROS:
• Lightweight, 10lbs +/-
• No tools or setup required. Screw the hitch onto your seatpost with the T-bold and you’re done.
• Folds to easily fit in a backseat, a trunk or an airline overhead.
• Holds up to $125 in groceries with the large hamper attached. Mind the maximum weight restriction (60lbs) and pack the heaviest items at the bottom (66% of load) and lighter items at the top (33%).
• With the Travoy you don’t have to bend over quite as far to reach cargo.
• Comes with a storage/carrying bag (although it’s mostly useless for carrying cargo).

CONS:
• You must adjust your riding style slightly. The Travoy is stable on level pavement but may tip over at significant road imperfections or surface debris. Slow down and approach handicapped ramps and driveways exactly at 90 degrees (perpendicular) to avoid catching a wheel on their raised shoulders. Avoid potholes and debris entirely. You’ll grow accustomed to this over time and it will not bother you. If the Travoy DOES tip, it doesn’t take the bike with it.
• If you run with the stock tires and tubes be prepared for flats. The availability of high quality 12.5” inch tires and tubes is extremely limited. All the tires from Asia that we tried are no good, even dangerous. We found very high quality 12.5 inch tires from the German manufacturer “Schwalbe” (available here on Amazon). Schwalbe currently offers the “Road Cruiser” for street and the “Black Jack” for trails and off-road (12/2020).
• 12.5” thorn resistant tubes are available here on Amazon but the Travoy 12.5 inch wheels require a 45 degree valve; otherwise there is not enough room to attach a pump or even a pump hose. These thorn resistant tubes had straight valves. To accommodate this shortcoming we found a "Air Inflator Hose Adapter" here on Amazon. Although it just barely fits, we can use it with both our floor pump and our road pump.

TIPS:
• In addition to thorn resistant tubes, we use the “Mr. Tuffy”-brand tire inserts on all our bike and trailer wheels (here on Amazon). Flats are now a very rare occurrence and we ride among numerous desert thorns.
• When using the hamper it is easy to cut a neon yellow reflective vest into three sections (left front, right front and back) and attach the sections to the hamper (left side, right side and rear, see photo).
• Reflective flags and flagpoles with mounts that fit your hamper are available here on Amazon. The flagpole we bought is high enough so that the flag can be seen above the level of a parked car (see photo). For added safety we now use this flag and pole on our bikes even without the trailer.
• When the hamper is inappropriate we use a cargo net. The cargo net is also handy if your hamper is overflowing.

Leave a comment if you have questions.
text_fidelity_b: Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer

text_fidelity_a:
Wallke X3 Pro Electric Bike Adults Folding 750W Fat Tire 32MPH eBike 20AH 48V Samsung Battery 26 Inch Mountain Electric Bicycle Full Suspension Shimano 8 Speed I wanted to have something that I could roll around town.

Since this was going to be my point of entry, I wanted something on the affordable end of the spectrum. I use the term affordable loosely. Spending $2K is not an easy decision when you have to be budget conscientious. But compared to some of the other off road bikes out there like the $6K ebikes, this fell somewhere in the middle of the pack.

That being said, I also needed it to be capable. So with that in mind, I knew that I wanted at least a 750W motor and ample run time. So the 14.5 battery pack was a deciding factor for me. And big tires with front and rear suspension to soak up some of the rugged terrain.

This bike arrived decently packaged, but still got some damage through shipping. There were also some minor defects that made it past QC. So there was some incomplete powder coating, some scrapped powder coating. And some bent spokes because the front wheel is shipped with the pedal sticking through them.

The entire assembly is a breeze and they even provide most of the tools needed. Only tool you will need of your own is a socket for the headlight bolt.

While having a folding bike might seem like a great feature for travel storage, it was not a concern for me since I just put the whole bike on a 2" hitch cargo basket. That being said, folding and unfolding this bike is a cinch using the sizable locking lever and retainer.

The thumb throttle on the left handle is easy to operate. Stepping up and down the three PAS levels works well. The throttle is not instant on. The start and stop delay is due to use of a cadence sensor. It's minor and not bothersome. The rear brakes hand lever is also on the left side. The brakes also cutoff the motor so you're not fighting the motor as you brake. I swapped the brake hoses so the right is rear and left is front. The brake cut off connector did not need to be swapped.

The center display is bright and easy to read in the sunlight. All the information is clear and well laid out. Accessing the advanced menu is done through pressing multiple buttons at the same time. This display looks a lot nicer than the standard LCD displays found on most ebikes.

As for the overall weight, it's a heavy bike. With tires that rival that of a small car and an 14AH battery pack, that's expected.

The tires have tiny tread blocks with just a small bit of side bite on the edges. Not sure how many ply the walls have. They seem to grip pretty well and ride softly. I've put them at 30PSI as recommended.

Update: The customer service support have been responsive and helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Wallke X3 Pro Electric Bike Adults Folding 750W Fat Tire 32MPH eBike 20AH 48V Samsung Battery 26 Inch Mountain Electric Bicycle Full Suspension Shimano 8 Speed

TRENDBOX Portable Outdoor 11 LED Camping Flashlight Bright Night Lamp Light Lantern Emergency for Hiking Fishing Tent with Hanging Hook I received this as a free review sample. When it arrived it was a lot smaller than I expected (2.6 x 1.8 x approximately 5 inches). However, when I inserted the required AA batteries and hit the power button I was very surprised by the amount of illumination it puts out. Even a brightly lit room this adds even more light. Do note that the AA batteries are not included.

One of the reasons this works so well is the reflector that makes maximum use of the light put out by the LED arrangement. I did test it at night as well and it worked perfectly on my enclosed patio. I could actually read by it in an otherwise dark room. If there is a shortcoming, it's the actual level of brightness. You can ruin your night vision by looking directly into it. It's best used as an overhead. Plus since the part that houses the reflector and LED is clear all around, it's not directional and can affect night vision of anyone on a space like a camping tent unless you take care in where you hang or place it.

I am not sure how waterproof this lantern is. The battery compartment is in the bottom and there appears to be no seal to keep out any water (and I did not test it). Hanging or off the floor it should not be a problem, but if you are looking for an emergency light that must withstand the elements this is probably not what you want. If you intend to use it as depicted - an overhead in a tent or hanging camping lantern - this is a handy light source. For me I have mine in a drawer for occasional in home use for then we lose power (a too common event in central Florida). It's small enough to stay out of the way, but functional enough to provide a nice amount of light when needed.
text_fidelity_b: TRENDBOX Portable Outdoor 11 LED Camping Flashlight Bright Night Lamp Light Lantern Emergency for Hiking Fishing Tent with Hanging Hook

text_fidelity_a: Coleman Camping Tent with Instant Setup, 4/6/8/10 Person Weatherproof Tent with Integrated Rainfly, Double-Thick Fabric, and Included Carry Bag, Sets Up in 60 Seconds This tent was packaged well. Easy to follow directions and was very simple to set up. I am an Eagle Scout and have been camping for over 35 years so the tent was pretty intuitive to set up. It says "Weathertec - guarenteed to keep you dry" on the outside. I read everything for sealing instructions prior to taking this to the woods. No requirements for sealing included and in fact it said all seams taped. I felt pretty confident. The weekend was calling for temps in the 50's and rain (not hard... just drizzle). I opened and tested the setup prior to camp. It was easy and seemed large enough. I took it out and had it set in approximately 30 seconds. The tent was spacious for two 6'2 guys and gear (cots) sleeping gear small packs and room to spare. It was shorter than expected and a bit smaller than I hoped... topping off about 5'5" at a guess and very tight with a cot (it touched the wall on both ends). The worst was the rain. It held up well to the first 1/2 hour or so but soon it was leaking. By 2am... it was damp... by morning there was about a cup of water in the floor. And the walls were soaked. The bathtub floor retained all the water. It leaked very badly. From seemingly every pore. The second night I spent alone in the dead center. Sleeping bag was soaked the tent was soaked and everything I had was damp even though it was in a chair or on a cot. It took over a day to dry the tent out to ship it back. All this from a light drizzle. Less than 1/2 inch of rain over two days. The firewood on the ground outside was dryer than the personals in my tent. On a scale of 1-10 Ease of set up 10, keeping out bugs 10, big windows 10... this could be a great shelter on a clear day but waterproof 1.

It’s been years since I played Ping Pong and back then I never had the opportunity to use, and was not even familiar with the Joola brand unfortunately. Each of these paddles have been designed for a specific purpose which include speed, spin and control. Now not being a professional, I can not “honestly” say that I notice the difference between any of these five different paddles, in any of the different design aspects while using them. Overall I feel quite privileged to have had the opportunity to use and experience the Joola brand and share my opinions, though I feel absolutely unqualified to have done so. text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) I want so badly to give this 5-stars. I am settling with 3 for now. Here's why:
Pros-
This is my first fitness tracker. I like that it measures my heart beat and steps- the exercise mode is nice too. I LOVE that I can sync it with my phone to have a vibrated notification of calls/caller ID and that it also does silent alarms. These features have been quickly integrated into my daily routine and I LOVE them!

Cons-
My first complaint comes about the mobile app. I have an android phone. My son has the CHARGE fitbit, and for some reason his app tells how long it takes him to fall asleep (minor difference, I will admit, but...) the app, while displaying the stats info from your tracker, as well as compiling averages for periods of time, doesn't give suggestions on how to modify your routine. The website offers a "premium" service, which gives you more detailed analysis, but I'm not sure it will also provide those missing helpful suggestions.
My second, and biggest complaint is the battery. I saw one reviewer experienced a similar issue with their fitbit and I can say after a mere 9 days of use, I can barely go 24hrs without a low battery notice, it's going back. I have been in touch with fitbit customer support today, and they seem to.be on top of things, but if I don't get a response I'm happy with, I'll have to try something else. My son has a refurbished fitbit charge, and it is working VERY well. I wanted us to be able to continue to run challenges ( he's 9, so keeping up with his 12,000 steps a day is an EXCELLENT GOAL for me!) But if I have to switch brands, I guess I will. Will update this review as soon as something changes!

Update! 11 months later:
I am so disappointed with my entire fitbit experience. I purchased another HR finding a better deal elsewhere after my original band quit working on me and I returned it to amazon. I should have quit while I was ahead. I have had 3 replacements, first 2 had issues with the internal functions and quit working. The 3rd fell apart. I do not wear in the shower, avoid getting it wet, or leaving damp after sweating even a little. I finally gave up and asked fitbit to do something- their response, I could have ANOTHER charge hr OR throw away my original $$$ and purchase ANOTHER Fitbit product at 30% off. Seriously?! I didn't have any of the trackers for more than 4 months each and they wanted me to replace their failed product by PAYING MORE for a replacement. No way! Throughly disgusted. Please, if you don't have disposable income to keep paying to replace these, look elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) Purchased this for my wife for Christmas, but I have given it to her early because she is concerned about heart rate and sleeping patterns.This review is a bit premature in light of the fact that I have yet to get any feedback from her on things life comfort and accuracy. But I thought I would try to help out others who are considering purchase of this item.

1. So far, out of the box it seems to be working properly.
2. There is no manual with the item. I found one on the Amazon site as part of the item description. If you wish to print the manual, the needed part is 19 pp.
3. You have the choice of using the fitbit with a smartphone or a puter. My wife is using it with her phone, which makes it highly portable with stats available on the phone app.
4. The battery in the unit is apparently NOT replaceable -- at least the manual offers no info on this point.
5. With normal use, the batt charge will last for 5 days. It can be recharged only one way, via USB port on a puter. There is no power cord, other than the USB cord that comes with the unit. I charged it and it took about an hour to reach full charge.
6. Now this is important if you don't want to wind up torturing yourself, as happened to me: REMOVE the piece of plastic that covers the watch crystal on the fitbit. The plastic piece is black and has a useless number on it. When you do the phone setup, the pairing with bluetooth will provide you with a 4-digit code. You cannot see the code unless you remove that piece of plastic protector.

Once my wife lets me know how the unit is doing, I will update this review with additional info. I hope you find this preliminary info helpful!
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

text_fidelity_a:
Continental Hometrainer Folding Tire I spent too much time reading about trainer tires and couldn't get any solid sense of a consensus, even an internet consensus. The best I was able to do was notice that people endorsing this tire gave cogent arguments for why they liked it; so I figured at least good critical thought was filtering opinions on these.

My experience is that it works great on the trainer. I have no other trainer tire for comparison; but compared with a road tire (Specialized Turbo Pro) it is night and day better. It grips better (e.g. sprints), is quieter... I guess that's enough.

I did get a tire bead jack to install it, but after the valve failed on the antique tube I was using, I was able to get this tire re-seated with my fingers. So maybe just the first installation is hard?

If you are like I was, combing through endless, non-comparative reviews of trainer tires, STOP RIGHT NOW AND BUY THIS ONE. It works great. There may be one that is better by some criterion over a very long period of time, but there is nothing wrong with this tire. I can't imagine any improvement. It even costs less than a typical road tire.

More advice: I thought it was frivolous to assemble a wheel just for the trainer but now I regret not doing it sooner. They have very cheap, serviceable wheels - and great prices on better wheels - right here on Amazon. I recommend keeping a separate wheel for the trainer so there is no disincentive for switching back and forth between indoors/out - and maybe more importantly, no incentive for buying another bike.
text_fidelity_b: Continental Hometrainer Folding Tire

text_fidelity_a: Dsoon Trail Camera 4K 32MP Deer Cameras The first trail cam we ever purchased, while we were not trying to be cheap about it, because of our lack of experience at the time with trail cams, we also didn't want to spend a ton but the first one we had was around $129 and it was absolutely a joke.  The night vision on that cam couldn't have possibly been worse, unless it just didn't work at all, but it worked slightly, however definitely not good enough for $129.  The picture quality was that of a child's first camera, to say the least.  So we decided to give this Dsoon a try.  This impressive set, at the time of purchase also had a $10 coupon , making this trail cam $69 and I was willing to give this is a try after reading some reviews and considering it was half of what we spent on our first one.  Right out of the box, this trail cam is aesthetically cool and very sturdy, the camo makes it great for hiding on most of our trails.  Very impressed with the fact that it comes with the 32gb card and card reader.  I feel like what's most impressive about this trail cam is the quality video, not only is it extremely clear and detailed, but the sound and visual 4K is just beautiful.  The resolution is quite impressive, and definitely blows our first one out of the water on most aspects.  Motion detection is also extremely impressive.  Keep in mind, all of these features are subject to placement, so just know that you will need stable, line of sight.  In other words your quality of sound and video, along with performance is only going to be as good as your choice of placement.  I had a friend that wasn't particularly aware of height when placing their trail camera outside their back door and she didn't place it high enough and a racoon easily got it and destroyed it, so always be mindful of that.  You really can't go wrong with this little trail cam and again for the price, it's absolutely worth it.  This would make a great gift for any outdoors person as well.  I hope this review is helpful!
text_fidelity_b: Dsoon Trail Camera 4K 32MP Deer Cameras

EST. 2017 Steel Tip Darts Set - Professional Darts Steel Tip for Dartboard - Includes Brass Barrels + Plastic & Aluminum Shafts + Rubber O'Rings + Flights + Darts Sharpener + Wrench I ordered the 'Professional Steel Tip Darts Set - USA American Flag and Patriotic Bald Eagle Inspired Colors - Customizable Configuration 6 Steel Tip Darts |Shafts |Standard Flights | O-Rings | Darts Tool| Sharpener' to review.

I have to say first off that I am not, nor have I ever been a professional Dart player. My experience has been purely recreational and to be honest, it's been close to 30 years since I really played. So when I had the opportunity to order and review this set, I was excited to give it a go. When I first opened this set I was absolutely blown away at the quality and options that come with this Dart set. The last time I played, I used plastic molded darts with dull steel tips. Btw, the steel tips with this set are nice and sharp out of the box!

This set has options. You can choose from the pre-installed aluminum flight shafts or the included plastic flight shafts. You can choose from standard flights, or the included smaller flights. The flights are a nice quality plastic and are a bit tricky to install at first as they are a really tight fit into flight shafts. The set also comes with extra O rings, a tip sharpening tool and a dart tool. What, a Dart tool? I never knew there was a such thing haha.

This is a great Dart set and though I am not a professional Dart player, I would most definitely consider this a professional set. The darts are well balanced and just feel solidly built. Overall I am very happy with this set and think it's a great value for the $$.
text_fidelity_b: SHOT TAKER CO. EST. 2017 Steel Tip Darts Set - Professional Darts Steel Tip for Dartboard - Includes Brass Barrels + Plastic & Aluminum Shafts + Rubber O'Rings + Flights + Darts Sharpener + Wrench

text_fidelity_a:
Britax Child Bike Seat (Prior Model) Britax has been making things for children for a very long time and it enjoys a strong reputation as a company that produces quality products. The high regard myself and others have for Britax was enough to convince me to obtain this bicycle seat and I have not regretted my decision.

I have two small girls, one of whom is still small enough to use a seat such as this. The weight limit is 40 pounds, so it is only going to work for children roughly four years of age or younger. My little one is still light enough and when she was first introduced, she took to this seat right away. She likes the adventurous feeling of riding on the back of the bicycle and I feel good knowing that she is safe and secure.

Looking at the specifics of this Britax bicycle seat, the seat is very sturdy in construction and it takes about 20 minutes from the box to the point where it is ready to use. It fits most all bicycles with 26 to 28 inch wheels, which would be just about every adult bicycle manufactured. It has a built in suspension for your child's comfort and this can be a great asset if the roads or sidewalks in your area are full of potholes and bumps. The headrest has nine position settings, the footrest has fifteen positions, and the harness locks securely in place, for maximum safety. The padding can be removed and is machine washable, for added convenience, and the product carries a limited two- year warranty.

Going for a spin with a child in a small seat behind you is quite an adventure and it does take getting used to. The added weight means you have to be more careful when you stop, when you start, and how you maneuver because you always have to be mindful of the child behind you and their safety. I admit that I was a little anxious when I used this at first, but my anxiety quickly faded when I started to ride. Once you get the hang of it, like anything, it gets easier. And it is very fun for the small child in the back who gets to enjoy the sites and the excitement of riding out in the open.

All things considered, I am hard pressed to find anything wrong with this bicycle seat and I recommend it for those with small children who like the adventure and fitness they receive from riding a bicycle. I would like to ride more, and perhaps this bicycle seat will encourage me to get more active. The seat is solid in construction, fairly easy to install, and made with safety in mind. It has all the earmarks of another quality Britax product and it earns a easy recommendation.
text_fidelity_b: Britax Child Bike Seat (Prior Model)
